newsitem.title: USA: NYMEX electricity higher on Pacific Intertie talk.
newsitem.headline: NYMEX electricity higher on Pacific Intertie talk.

text.p: NYMEX electricity futures were trading higher Friday on talk that capacity on the Pacific Intertie transmission system could be reduced in early July, industry sources said.
"The (Intertie) seems to be the only fundamental news out there," said one New York based futures trader.
Transmission capacity on the intertie may fall July 1 to 6,300 megawatts (MW), compared with the current limit of 7,200 MW, Bonneville Power Administration (BPA) said Thursday.
In the meantime, a Western Systems Coordinating Council committee is expected to propose next week a summertime rating for the intertie of 6,900 MW.

As of 1240 EDT, July Palo Verde (PV) was trading up $1.24 at the day's high of $28.00 per megawatt hour (MWh) following exchanges as low as $27.40, while August was up 94 cents at $29.85 after trades in a range of $29.50-30.00 per MWh.

July California Oregon Border (COB) was up 92 cents at $18.00 following trades in a range of $17.50-18.10, while August was up 46 cents at the day's high of $21.05 after trade as low as $20.90 per MWh.
NYMEX said as of 1145 EDT an estimated total of 61 COB and 224 PV contracts had traded.
Over 2,500 MW of generation was expected to return to service by next week.
The 750 MW unit 5 at the Four Corners coal-fired power plant in New Mexico was expected to return to service by Monday following a shutdown late Thursday.

Also, several Western coal-fired power units began restarting yesterday, including a 450 MW San Juan unit in New Mexico, a 300 MW Reid Gardner unit in Nevada, a 190 MW Hayden unit in Colorado and a 670 MW Centralia unit in Washington.
In addition, the 1,112 MW WNP-2 nuclear power plant in Washington state was expected to resume power production next week, ahead of an original schedule.
Meanwhile, a 875 MW unit at the Intermountain coal-fired power plant in Utah is said to shut today through Sunday to repair a tube leak.
Meterologists called for temperatures across the West next week to run slightly above-normal with precipitation averaging near to above-normal.

Main cities along the West Coast from Seattle down to San Diego would see readings in the 70s Fahrenheit area, while those in the interior Southwest such as Phoenix and Tucson would experience weather in the 90s.
As of 1240 EDT, July NYMEX Henry Hub natural gas futures were trading up 6.4 cents at $2.144 per million British thermal units.
